observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a swirled hard-candy lollipop (yellow, teal-blue, white, with a green region on its right side) mounted on a white stick, held against a dark blurred background of stones and a flat surface. A blue flame is visible at the right edge, directed toward the candy. The green portion on the right is already glossy and partially melted at the start of the excerpt.
visible_changes: The green melted mass on the right side of the lollipop gradually becomes more textured/foamy and slightly larger, extending further down and right over the segment (smooth tongue in early frames vs. bubbly mass in later frames).
A small green droplet detaches from the lower tip of the melted green region around t=0.43 s (visible as a separate hanging drop) and is gone by t=0.47 s, indicating it fell out of frame.
The blue flame at the right edge becomes brighter and more clearly defined in the later half of the excerpt compared to the faint glow at the start.
The main swirled body of the lollipop, its stick, and the background surface/stones remain in essentially fixed positions; no camera pan/zoom is evident.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the melting/dripping began before this segment or continues after it (the green melt is already present at t=0 and still present at the end).
The source or setup of the flame and the heating apparatus (only the flame's glow is visible).
Where the detached droplet landed or whether more drops fall later.
uncertain_details: Exact size change of the green mass is small and partly confounded by shifting highlights/reflections on the wet surface.
The apparent growth in flame intensity could be due to flame behavior or to slight changes in exposure/reflection; not certain.
Whether the green region's lower tip truly translates downward or merely changes shape as it melts.
